layers.label: Onion-shell structure
layers.explanation: The star's fused layers, arranged like an onion: hydrogen outer shell, then heavier and heavier elements inward, ending in the iron core at the center.

layers.label: Expanding blast shell
layers.explanation: The envelope flying outward after the shock breaks through — the supernova remnant, glowing as it cools.

hotspots.label: Iron core — the fuse
hotspots.description: The center of the massive star where fusion builds iron — the one fuel that takes energy to fuse, so nothing can hold the core up anymore.

hotspots.label: Infalling envelope
hotspots.description: With no fusion energy left to hold them, the star's outer layers fall inward at a good fraction of light speed.

hotspots.label: Rebound shockwave
hotspots.description: The compressed core bounces back like a spring, sending a shock wave outward that shreds the star apart in one brilliant blow.

hotspots.label: Expanding remnant shell
hotspots.description: The supernova remnant — hot expanding gas and freshly forged heavy elements that will seed the next generation of stars.

hotspots.label: Element forge
hotspots.description: Blast heat and speed build the heaviest elements — gold, silver, uranium, the very atoms of your body.

visualStyleNotes: Timeline-driven scene (no auto-rotate; user drags the Play slider). Onion-shell star with a faint iron-gray core; blast goes off in a cool blue-white shell, then a warm violet remnant cloud expands. Anatomy Atelier warm whites and soft beams throughout, nothing stark.
materialNotes: Star envelopes: translucent tinted shells (white, gold, cold blue); core: dark umber with violet rim. Shockwave ring: bright cyan wire-rim. Remnant cloud: translucent violet, soft noise texture, no opacity modulation over time.
assetBrief: Procedural Three.js scene on a timeline controlled by a slider: onion-layered star (5 shells), collapse (shells descend inward), bounce ring emission, expanding remnant sphere. Element counter in the UI counts gold/silver/uranium. Hotspot beads (~0.16) present on all listed ids.
